_comment: Which pages of the Book set type over a plate, and what the check holds them to.
Read by scripts/whitepaper-plates/check_cover_title_band.py; see that file's
docstring for the two halves and why the thresholds are what they are.
Pages are NOT listed by number. A page number in a 550-page book that is
rebuilt on every push is a maintenance burden that goes stale silently, and
the rule we actually want is not 'page 279 must be legible' but 'any page
that sets type over a plate must be legible'. So each edition declares a
scope, and the check discovers the pages: every page carrying an image over
min_plate_page_fraction of its area is measured, and every line of type that
lands inside that image is held to the contrast floor.
The covers additionally carry a plate-only floor, because that one can be
checked with no build at all -- it is what stops a plate being committed in
the first place, before there is a PDF to read.
WCAG 2.2 AA: 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text (>= 18pt, or 14pt
bold). The ground under a line is not one colour -- it is a watercolour
wash, a halftone, a colour plane -- so the ratio is computed against the
10th percentile of the ground's luminance inside the line's own bounding
box: the darker end of what the glyphs actually cross, not the average,
which a small dark passage would hide.
Measured on the corpus the day this landed: every line that reads cleanly
sits at 6.4:1 or better (the maritime cover's worst is 9.75:1, the fresh
Swiss cover's imprint 6.43:1). The lines that are genuinely hard to read
sit at 2.6-3.7:1. The AA floor lands between them without tuning.
This replaced an ink-share test (fail above 8% inked pixels under a line).
That test worked on the hard-edged covers and was wrong for the
watercolour part openers, where a pale wash inks a lot of pixels and is
perfectly readable. Contrast against the type's own colour is the
question; ink share was a proxy for it that only held on two pages.

_editions_comment: The page half of this check reads built PDFs, so it registers the editions
that are built -- one. The Book's typographic character is chosen by
the canonical coordination-papers-mega-volume.pdf renders it; Swiss is the
central edition today. The maritime and technical drivers stay in the tree
and build on demand, but nothing publishes them, so registering them here
would ask this check to read a PDF no build produces -- and check_pages
treats a registered edition with no built PDF as a failure, correctly.
Making one of them central again is a one-line move in the preamble plus
the matching id and note below.
The covers below are a separate register: their half measures the plate
files, which are all still in the tree, so it keeps guarding every
character's cover with no build at all.

editions.note: The central edition, rendered into the canonical Book PDF. The cover is full-bleed photomontage with the type at fixed TikZ coordinates; part plates take the room left below the type.

covers.note: Full-bleed jacket, type placed by a \vspace* from the top margin.
Full-bleed photomontage, type placed at absolute TikZ coordinates.
